prerequisites: Attainment of the second study section (at least 42 ECTS points from the first study section)
Proficient use of the Java programming language
Proficient use of matrices, determinants, and linear transformations

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the most important concepts, algorithms, and methods of computer graphics and apply fundamental computer graphics techniques.
Understand the purpose of Bézier curves, B-Splines, NURBS, and use them in applications.
Name components of 3D modeling and use 3D modeling techniques.
Apply surface representation techniques depending on the problem.
Name and use various algorithms for visibility decisions.
Apply techniques for lighting, shading, and shadow effects.
Use different mappings for texture representation.
Generate simple computer-simulated 3D worlds and render them with self-created software.
Understand the connection between the components of the rendering pipeline.
Execute application-oriented programming tasks in the field of computer graphics in Java.

syllabus_topics: 2D Graphics and Rasterization: Coordinate systems, Line representation, Aliasing, Polygon rasterization, Clipping, Transformations
3D Modeling: Scene graph, Volume modeling, Normal cells, Octrees, CSG, Edge and surface modeling, Wireframe model
Surface Representation: Topological structure, Euler operations, Surfaces, Polygons, Bilinear interpolation, Coon's Patch, Free-form surfaces
Transformations and Projections: Affine transformations, Perspective and projective mappings
3D World to 2D Device Coordinates: View transformation, Projection transformation, Clipping, Normalization, Screen transformation
Visibility Decision: 3D clipping, Back-face culling, Depth buffer algorithm, List-Priority method, Scan-Line method, Raycasting
Lighting and Shading: Ambient, diffuse, specular reflection, Distance dependence, Fog, Shading, Transparency
Shadow Calculation: Shadow volume, Shadow depth buffer
Textures: Texture Mapping, Texture coordinate system, Two-Pass Mapping, Environment Mapping, Bump Mapping, Aliasing
assessment_rules: Passing the practical lab (21.2) is a prerequisite for participation in the main computer graphics course (21.1). Successful submission of 5 practical assignments via the automatic test system is required for the practical lab.
